claim.excerpt: It was worth mentioning that there was a linear rise in vitreous potassium concentration with advancing PMI, which was first described by Sturner in 1963.

sources.title: Estimation of postmortem interval by vitreous potassium evaluation with a novel fluorescence aptasensor.

why_it_matters: A marker claim can be used to support time-since-death or exposure reasoning.

conflicts.question: Can vitreous potassium be used to estimate the post-mortem interval?
conflicts.note: One source reports a linear rise of vitreous potassium with advancing PMI; another reports an inconsistent influence of temperature and calls it a potential confounding factor.
